title: How many labelers do you have? A closer look at gold-standard labels: continuity of the optimizing direction in a semiparametric majority-vote M-estimator
author: Chen Cheng, Hilal Asi, John Duchi
work: How many labelers do you have? A closer look at gold-standard labels
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Lemma (source0.tex lines 4325--4329, source label lemma:vec-sigma-theta-continuity): as the L2(P) distance between the tuple of m link functions and the true link tuple tends to 0, the optimizing direction theta-star of the semiparametric majority-vote M-estimator converges to the true direction u-star; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 4330--4404 (one adjacent proof environment of 75 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span. It reduces, through the retained support lemma lemma:super-generic-solutions (lines 4231--4255, whose statement identifies the minimizer theta-star = t u-star with t the unique zero of the calibration gap h), to showing that t converges to 1; it expands m h(t) into a perturbation term plus the exact gap of the true links; it isolates the perturbation with a nested Claim (claim:taco, lines 4345--4389, proved in full inside the same retained proof) whose argument splits the L2(P) integral at 0 < M_0 < M_1, uses continuity and positivity of the density of |Z| on (0, infinity) to bound the density ratio p(z)/p(z-prime) uniformly on [M_0/2, 2 M_1], applies the substitution tz -> z to bound the inner integral by sqrt(2) times the L2(P) distance, and then lets M_0 decrease to 0 and M_1 increase to infinity; and it finishes by showing that each true-link component f_j(t) has strictly positive derivative, so that t = 1 is its unique zero and t must converge to 1. Every display the proof references is either retained or proved in place, and the only external input is the retained support lemma. H2: an original research-level stability/continuity lemma whose proof combines a uniform-integrability (truncation and density-ratio) argument with the implicit monotonicity of the population gap function, and which is the technical step that lets the article's semiparametric master theorem be applied to estimated link functions; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
